paper.title: Non-Asymptotic Pure Exploration by Solving Games

settings.name_in_paper: Pure exploration (fixed confidence, delta-PAC) in K-armed bandits with one-parameter exponential family arms
unmapped: General pure exploration query: model set M, finite answer set I, correct-answer function i^*(mu) (covers Best Arm Identification and Minimum Threshold)
Fixed confidence delta-PAC: algorithm must be delta-correct; objective is expected stopping time
Model M contained in [mu_min, mu_max]^K (Assumption 2), sub-Gaussian exponential family (Assumption 1)
settings.definition_quote: A pure exploration problem is parameterised by a set $\mathcal M$ of $K$-armed bandit models (the possible environments), a finite set $\mathcal I$ of candidate answers and a correct-answer function $i^* : \mathcal M {\to} \mathcal I$. ... An algorithm is $\delta$-PAC (or $\delta$-correct) if $\pr_\vmu(\ihat \neq i^*(\vmu)) \le \delta$ for each $\vmu \in \mathcal M$. Among $\delta$-PAC algorithms, we are interested in those minimising the sample complexity $\ex_\vmu[\tau_\delta]$.

algorithms.name: Pure exploration meta-algorithm (Algorithm 1: GLRT stopping + two no-regret learners + optimism + tracking)

conditions: threshold beta(t,delta) satisfies P_mu{GLR_t({mu}) > beta(t,delta)} <= delta
tuning: GLRT stopping and recommendation rules with threshold beta(t,delta)

source.label: th:GLRT_delta_correct
source.quote: Any algorithm using the GLRT stopping and recommendation rules with threshold $\beta(t,\delta)$ such that $\pr_\vmu\{\mbox{GLR}_t^{\Theta^K}(\{\vmu\}) > \beta(t, \delta)\}\leq \delta$ is $\delta$-correct.

results.notes: Holds for any sampling rule with GLRT stopping; attached to Algorithm 1. Standard result (Garivier & Kaufmann 2016) restated; marked as paper's theorem.

bound.expression_latex: \ex_\vmu[\tau_\delta] \leq T_0(\delta) + \frac{2eK}{a^2}, T_0(\delta) = \max \{t\in\N: t \leq \frac{\beta(t,\delta)}{D_\vmu} + C_\vmu(R_t^\vlambda + R_t^k + h(t))\}

symbols.T_0: max{t : t <= beta(t,delta)/D_mu + C_mu (R_t^lambda + R_t^k + h(t))}
symbols.D_mu: value of the pure exploration game (characteristic time inverse)
symbols.C_mu: instance-dependent constant depending on mu and M
symbols.R_t^k: regret bound of the k-player learner
symbols.R_t^lambda: regret bound of the lambda-player learner

conditions: Assumption 2: M subset of [mu_min,mu_max]^K inside Theta
arms in a one-parameter exponential family (sub-Gaussian)

source.label: th:sample_complexity
source.quote: Under Assumption~\ref{ass:compact_M}, the sample complexity of Algorithm~\ref{alg:the_algorithm} on model $\vmu\in\mathcal{M}$ is $\ex_\vmu[\tau_\delta] \leq T_0(\delta) + \frac{2eK}{a^2}$ with $T_0(\delta) = \max \{t\in\N: t \leq \frac{\beta(t,\delta)}{D_\vmu} + C_\vmu(R_t^\vlambda + R_t^k + h(t))\}$, where $C_\vmu$ depends on $\vmu$ and $\mathcal{M}$ and $h(t) = \mathcal{O}(\sqrt{t\log(t)})$.

results.notes: Implicit bound via T_0. Applies to instantiations such as AdaHedge vs Best-Response (Lemma 3: R_t^k = O(sqrt(t ln K) ln t), R^lambda <= 0) and FTPL (R^lambda = O(sqrt(t log t))). Asymptotically optimal as delta->0.

bound.expression_latex: T_0(\delta) + \frac{2eK}{a^2}, T_0(\delta) = \max\{t: t \leq (\beta(t,\delta) + h(t))/D_\vmu\}, h(t) = 2\sqrt{t}D_\vmu + 3L\sqrt{2\sigma^2 f(t)}(K^2 + (2\sqrt{2}+1/3)\sqrt{Kt}) + f(t)(K^2 + 2K\log(t/K)) + KD

symbols.T_0: maximal t in N with t <= (beta(t,delta)+h(t))/D_mu, h as in the statement
symbols.D_mu: value of the pure exploration game
symbols.L_d: Lipschitz constant of x -> d(x,y) on [mu_min,mu_max] (paper's L)

source.quote: Take $b=1$ in the definition of $f(t)$. Let $h(t) = 2\sqrt{t}D_\vmu + 3L\sqrt{2\sigma^2 f(t)}(K^2 + (2\sqrt{2}+\nicefrac{1}{3})\sqrt{Kt}) + f(t)(K^2 + 2K\log(t/K)) + KD$. Then the expected sample complexity is at most $T_0(\delta) + \frac{2eK}{a^2}$, where $T_0(\delta)$ is the maximal $t\in\N$ such that $t \leq (\beta(t,\delta) + h(t))/D_\vmu$ .

results.notes: Requires a max-max-min oracle per step. Implicit bound via T_0.
